A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HOLO and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–10, Figures 1–11, and supplementary sections A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HOLO localization experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse, together with ablations, robustness tests, segmentation results, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original HOLO experiments and analyses, including the nuScenes results in Table 1 and Argoverse results in supplementary Table 10.

M1.justification: The architecture, homography-guided correlation, iterative refinement, pose recovery, and objectives remain unchanged. Equation (7) now explicitly sums semantic losses across modalities, but this combination was already defined in v1's supplementary Equation (12) and evaluated in Table 9.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes and Argoverse with corresponding OSM maps. The road/drivable-area supervision, resolution and noise scenarios, and qualitative nighttime and rainy-weather examples are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same OrienterNet, U-BEV, MapLocNet variants, SegLocNet variants, and HOLO-CA comparisons; Table 10 retains MapLocNet. The added HCNet and SSHNet mentions in Section 3.4 are methodological citations, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated nuScenes training count from 850 to 700 scenes while retaining 150 validation scenes. This is a limited reported protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or the earlier description was corrected. Other settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The homography-head, iteration, feature-fusion, semantic-loss, resolution/noise, and runtime analyses are retained. Supplementary section E also contains the same segmentation examples, map-alignment analysis, and three failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their entries and numerical values, and the plotted and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains HOLO-drivable position Recall@1m/2m of 36.41%/61.21%, and Table 10 retains HOLO's Argoverse values of 29.38%/51.89%. No performance gain between versions is reported.

T1.justification: The homography equations and pose derivations are unchanged. The explicit modality sum added to Equation (7) restates the semantic-loss definition already present in supplementary Equation (12), rather than introducing new mathematics. No assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint semantic and homography learning, localization accuracy, convergence and inference efficiency, cross-resolution support, and the nuScenes SD-map extension.

C2.justification: The explanations of geometric guidance, semantic alignment, and computational efficiency remain unchanged. The appendix retains the same limitations involving map inaccuracies, sparse road-direction cues, dense traffic, and ambiguous map structures.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a generic code-and-model release promise with a HOLO GitHub hyperlink, providing a concrete access location. Release wording remains future tense, so actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Hardware, hyperparameters, and implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 expands its stated methodological inspiration from IHN alone to IHN, HCNet, and SSHNet. HCNet and SSHNet were already cited elsewhere in v1, so this is a limited refinement of attribution and positioning. Bibliographic metadata changes do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and notation edits, clarifies the main-text semantic-loss expression, adds a funding acknowledgement, and updates some bibliography metadata. The main section order, supplementary structure, and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The figures and tables retain their content and organization. There are limited equation-spacing and text-flow adjustments, reference reflow following the new acknowledgement, and removal of printed page-number footers.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity by making Equation (7) consistent with the existing appendix definition, broadens explicit methodological attribution, and supplies a concrete repository link. These are modest documentation gains. The empirical evidence is unchanged, and the unexplained 850-to-700 training-count revision leaves uncertainty about the experimental history, limiting the overall improvement.
